inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 16th February, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) warned today of active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds, raising dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 3,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The Centre stated in a statement issued today that the weather conditions began at 10:30 and will continue until 18:00, urging the public to exercise caution, particularly when driving on external and open roads, due to the risk of sudden drops in visibility caused by blowing dust.

requested_area.areaDesc: Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)

fields.description: EXERCISE - Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand, reducing visibility to under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi. Until 18:00 today, 16 Feb 2026. Source: NCM.
fields.headline: EXERCISE: Blowing dust reducing visibility in coastal and inland Abu Dhabi until 18:00
fields.instruction: Take care, especially when driving on external and open roads, as visibility can drop suddenly. More: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was left out for that reason.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I set severity to Moderate and urgency to Immediate because NCM reports ongoing conditions (10:30-18:00) with visibility under 3,000 m, and the source gives no time zone (assumed local). NCM says only 'some' coastal and inland areas, while the target area was chosen by the operator, so please confirm that this alert really is exercise-only before release.

objections.fix: Remove 'Abu Dhabi' from the headline and description and use the bulletin's wording, for example 'Blowing dust reducing visibility in some coastal and inland areas of the UAE until 18:00' and '...reducing visibility to under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas.' Do not name a specific emirate unless NCM specifies one.
objections.issue: The alert places the hazard in 'coastal and inland Abu Dhabi'. The verified NCM bulletin names no emirate and refers only to 'some coastal and inland areas'. 'ABU DHABI' in the input is the WAM dateline, not the warning area. The alert therefore changes the places covered, and people in other affected areas may wrongly think the warning does not apply to them.

payload.summary: Hazard, times (until 18:00, 16 Feb 2026), visibility threshold, wind description, and the Moderate/Immediate/Observed codes match or are supported by the verified NCM bulletin. The alert does narrow the affected area to 'Abu Dhabi', which the bulletin does not say. 'ABU DHABI' is only the WAM news dateline; the NCM warning covers 'some coastal and inland areas' with no emirate named.

no_basis.concern: A drill alert with scope Public is being sent from a live console. People should confirm that Exercise-status messages reach only the UAE-Alert exercise channel and are not mistaken for a real alert. None of the clauses shown sets a rule for public-scope exercises on live systems.
no_basis.searched_for: Rule restricting the scope or channel of Exercise-status alerts sent from a live environment

The status is Exercise, which fits the EXERCISE / DRILL context, and the headline is marked EXERCISE. objections.fix: Add a short protective action right after the hazard in both languages, and put both at the very start. For example, EN: 'EXERCISE - Dust storm, visibility under 3 km, Abu Dhabi coast/inland: drive slowly, keep distance, avoid outdoor activity if you have breathing problems.' Give the matching Arabic wording, front-loaded so that 'غبار' (dust) and the action begin on page 1. Move the wind detail, end time and source after the action.
objections.issue: No protective action appears anywhere in either language, so the first page cannot carry the action. Both texts only describe the wind, dust and visibility, plus the end time and source. In Arabic, the first 41-character page holds only the exercise tag and 'strong northwesterly winds'; the dust and visibility hazard spills onto page 2.

However, neither language tells people what to do, so the first page carries the hazard but no protective action. The Arabic first page (41 UCS-2 characters) also shows only the exercise tag and the wind, not the dust or low visibility.

payload.summary: The Arabic matches the English in meaning on every point I checked. The EXERCISE marker تمرين appears in both the headline and the description. The hazard (northwesterly winds, active to occasionally strong, raising dust and sand) is the same. The figures match: visibility under 3,000 m, until 18:00 today, 16 Feb 2026. The areas match: coastal and inland Abu Dhabi. The protective action is the same: take care, especially when driving on external and open roads, because visibility can drop suddenly. The source (NCM) and the link are kept. I found no difference in meaning. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named Arabic-reading reviewer must still check and approve it before it is sent.

fields.description: EXERCISE - Blowing dust: visibility under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas. Drive with caution on external and open roads; visibility can drop suddenly. Northwesterly winds, occasionally strong, until 18:00 today, 16 Feb. Source: NCM.
fields.headline: EXERCISE: Blowing dust reducing visibility in some coastal and inland areas until 18:00
fields.instruction: Take extra care when driving, especially on external and open roads, because blowing dust can suddenly reduce visibility. Updates: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: 'Abu Dhabi' as the hazard location: it is the WAM dateline, not the warning area. The NCM bulletin names only 'some coastal and inland areas'.
'of the UAE' from the Met reviewer's example: the bulletin does not state the country or any emirate, so it was not added.

'Drive slowly, keep distance' and 'avoid outdoor activity if you have breathing problems' from the network reviewer's example: the verified bulletin only urges caution when driving on external and open roads. Health advice is not in the inputs.
Arabic phone text: this draft is English only, as instructed. The Arabic version, front-loaded with 'غبار' and the driving action on page 1, needs a separate translation.
Start time 10:30: dropped from the phone text for length. The hazard is already in progress.
fields.note_for_reviewer: The operator's target area is the Abu Dhabi demo zone, but the bulletin does not name an emirate, so the text uses the bulletin's 'some coastal and inland areas' wording; please confirm this suits the chosen polygon. I used only NCM's driving caution as the action and did not add the reviewers' extra health and driving advice, because it is not in the verified bulletin.

payload.summary: The alert matches the verified NCM bulletin. It names the same hazard: active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds raising dust, with visibility below 3,000 m. It covers the same places (some coastal and inland areas) and the same end time (until 18:00 on 16 Feb). It repeats the bulletin's driving caution about sudden visibility drops. Certainty 'Observed' fits because conditions began at 10:30. Moderate severity and Immediate urgency do not overstate the bulletin. Nothing in the alert comes from an unverified source.

no_basis.concern: The console environment is 'live' and scope is Public, so this Exercise alert may go out on live public channels. UAE cell broadcast does define a dedicated Exercise class (TDRA specs), so this may be intended. Approvers should still confirm that live public distribution of the drill is deliberate rather than a training-console mix-up, as in the Hawaii and Pickering incidents.
no_basis.searched_for: A UAE rule saying whether Exercise-status alerts may or may not be sent from the live environment to the public.

payload.summary: Within the issuing-authority mandate nothing is wrong. The sender demo-national-authority@nadhir.example is in the issuer register at level 1, covering all areas and categories, so it may issue a Met alert here. The alert's areaDesc and codes match the area drawn for event uae-dust-drill. Status is Exercise, which fits the EXERCISE / DRILL context, and the headline is prefixed EXERCISE. There are no active alerts from other authorities to overreach. msgType is Alert, so no reference to an earlier alert is needed.

no_basis.concern: The first page does not carry the action. At about 93 GSM-7 characters per page, the English page 1 ends mid-way through 'Drive with caution'. At 41 UCS-2 characters per page, the Arabic page 1 holds only the hazard and visibility ('تمرين - غبار متطاير: الرؤية أقل من 3,000 م'), and the action 'قُد بحذر' falls on a later page. A handset that shows only the first page would lose the action.
no_basis.searched_for: alert first page hazard action; TDRA cell broadcast handset Arabic English; 3GPP TS 23.041 page limit UCS-2. No returned clause requires the hazard and action to sit on the first page.

no_basis.concern: The Arabic is machine-translated. No UAE-specific rule was found that says whether machine-translated Arabic alert text is allowed, or what human review it needs before broadcast. The clauses returned are from FCC and CAP-CP, not UAE.

no_basis.concern: CAP-CP recommends flagging automated translation in the message. I cannot see the message parameters, so I cannot check whether the Arabic block is flagged as machine-translated. That check is outside my view.

The exercise label (تمرين) is present in the headline and description. Visibility under 3,000 m, the time 18:00, today 16 Feb, northwesterly winds that are occasionally strong, coastal and inland areas, and the source NCM all match. The protective action also matches: drive with extra caution on external and open roads because visibility can drop suddenly. The URL is unchanged. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named person who reads Arabic must still review and approve it before release. This review does not replace that approval.
